item.title: Mem0 vs Honcho: Fact Memory vs User Modeling
item.description:
Mem0 vs Honcho is a choice between remembering facts and understanding people. Mem0 pulls short facts out of conversations and returns the ones that match a query. Honcho keeps the full messages, runs background reasoning over them, and builds a model of each participant that your agent can ask questions about in plain language.

Both are open source and both have a managed service. They differ in license (Apache 2.0 vs AGPL-3.0), in how much LLM work happens after each write, and in how they treat multi-agent conversations. Many teams weighing the two also look at Hindsight, an MIT-licensed memory server that, like Honcho, reasons over memories in the background, and posts the highest vendor-reported scores of the three on LongMemEval and BEAM. Sources are each project’s README, docs, pricing page and published evals, checked on 12 October 2026.

item.title: Honcho LLM Memory: Peers, Reasoning and Setup
item.description:
Honcho is an open-source memory service for LLM agents, built by Plastic Labs. Instead of only storing extracted facts, it reasons about the people and agents in your conversations. You save messages; a background worker derives conclusions about each participant; then you ask Honcho what it knows, in plain language or as prompt-ready context.

This page covers Honcho’s data model, how its reasoning pipeline works, the Python SDK, self-hosting, pricing and its benchmark claims. Sources are the Honcho GitHub README, the Honcho docs and honcho.dev, checked on 8 October 2026.
